newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DOLLAR AND BUNDESBANK ENSNARE BELGIAN OLOS.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR AND BUNDESBANK ENSNARE BELGIAN OLOS.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures drifted in near-neutral territory on Friday afternoon, lacking the volume to go the one way dealers foresaw in the near term -- down.
Dealers noted some swapping out of OLOs into Bunds. Equally, there were reverse moves by players seeing some spread widening.

"We will be volatile next week," a trader said. The market was caught between the dollar, whose weakening supported the short end earlier, and the Bundesbank. The central bank itself is trapped between a soft mark whose image in the markets needs polishing and a weak economy preventing an interest rate hike.

"We are drifting, not aggressively, but we are drifting," a trader said, "there is still downside potential" mainly depending on key Bund futures FDBc1 holding above support at 101.58. The contracts posted a 101.63 low by late afternoon.
"If 101.58 is broken, it will look quite negative...we will break down to 101.42/29," he said.
He was not "mega-bearish", though. The 10-year OLO/Bund spread MEUR could at the most widen to 15 basis points. At Friday's high it had already been "reasonably wide."
By 1400 GMT it had come back in to nine basis points, unchanged from Thursday.
The U.S. currency slid further in the course of Friday, with profit-taking pushing it down to about 1.8550 marks.
Dealers said most players were trying to go into the weekend with flat positions. The market would remain cautious next week ahead of U.S. inflation and retail sales data US-ECI.

"With the dollar off its highs, the heat is off at the short end," a trader said. But another warned the Belgian franc had problems strengthening along with the mark "and therefore the money market problems are here to stay."
The franc continued to hover around the 20.65 level against the mark in late Friday afternoon trade.

Players were eyeing Treasuries USc1, which were suffering from interest rate fears after recent data showed the U.S. economy continued to power ahead, but Treasuries' weakness failed to drag OLOs down much.

Short OLOs were Friday's flavour as the dollar retreated vis a vis the mark. Some players said the slippage removed part of the market's concerns about a need for central bank action to keep inflationary pressures in check.
As the dollar dipped below 1.87 marks DEM=, interest flared up in switching down the curve. "They are swapping five (year OLOs) for two and then 10 for five," a trader said.

London currency analysts said that if the franc's weakness continued, Belgium might surprise the markets with an interest rate rise. But others wondered if Belgium -- particularly its exporters -- was not actually content to see a softer franc.
The only action from the Belgian National Bank so far has been to drain off liquidity repeatedly through its daily repurchase agreements, pushing market rates higher.

A bond trader said that fundamentally, it was only a matter of economic indicators showing signs of imported inflation before bond prices would start sliding. He foresaw the first rate hike within the next two months.
